review.reviewer: independent PH-279 cash-bridge-snapshot reviewer (fresh context, read-only)
findings: BLOCKER - module-disabled history read is not delivered at the HTTP boundary: PH-279 spec freezes 'cash 模块停用后只读历史可读', but domain_metadata marks both `cash_bridge_snapshot` and `cash_bridge_issues` as `business_read`, so the plugin runtime returns 403 after the cash module is disabled (test_module_disabled_http_routes_refuse_but_service_history_readable explicitly asserts 403). The service layer is readable, but the browser history page is part of the frozen read surface and the spec's history-read requirement is unmet; this is a real contract gap, not just a cosmetic note. Fix: register both read routes as `history_read` (the same pattern used by PH-275/PH-287) and change the HTTP regression to expect 200 after module disable while keeping POST 405/no write; keep the service-level read path as is.

READ-ONLY/AGGREGATION (otherwise verified): cash_bridge_snapshot/issues derive posted CashTransaction -> active CashClassification/reversal -> AccountingEvent -> LedgerPosting/bank_effect claim -> Refund/BankReturn -> InternalTransfer, plus classification_services.cash_book_coverage for account cash-book net (not bank balance); no audit/receipt/event/ledger/cash write, no migration, no verify_integrity change, no invented offset (offset_implemented=false); refund/return reverse cash is marked derived_cash and excluded from classification_missing; refund+return > gross, posting count/amount/book/scope, claim missing/net, transfer cross-org/leg/amount/date, event missing/duplicate and stale/reversed classification paths are covered; gold receipt and internal-transfer pair cases return issues=[]; scoped 13 OK. PM/member denial is the disclosed and acceptable response to cash facts having no project attribution (deny rather than leak org-wide cash). Non-blocking defensive gap: in `_transaction_issues` a tampered transaction with >1 active classification sets `classification=None`, so it would report classification_missing rather than classification_duplicate_active; the DB's unique active-classification constraint makes this unreachable in normal writes, but the intended duplicate-code branch is dead and untested.

Independent runs: check ok=212; manage check exit 0; makemigrations clean; scoped 13 OK; full suite 989/5F+3E/69 = known 8 macOS baseline; verify_integrity fresh DB ok; verify-change only high_risk_review_required, no path_out_of_scope. Read-only purity, classification->event->posting/claim aggregation, derived refund/return handling, refund/return <= gross, transfer pair/leg/amount/date/cross-org checks, cash_book_coverage net, offset_implemented=false, PM/member denial (disclosed, acceptable), no migration/write/verify_integrity change are otherwise verified. BLOCKER fix: set `cash_bridge_snapshot`/`cash_bridge_issues` route access to `history_read` and expect 200 after cash module disable, keeping POST 405/no write; non-blocking: the >1 active classification branch is unreachable and untested (DB unique constraint), and would misreport as classification_missing if ever reached.

deviations: PM access: the spec says pm may read only the cash-flow summary of projects they manage, but PH-239/240/245 cash facts (CashTransaction/FundingAccount/Refund/BankReturn/InternalTransfer/classification) carry no project attribution, so a project-scoped pm summary cannot be derived without leaking company-wide cash. This slice therefore denies pm (403) together with member rather than exposing org-wide cash, and discloses the spec/runtime mismatch for a future planning slot.

Module-disabled history read: the two bridge routes are registered as history_read (the same precedent as PH-275/PH-287), so after the cash module is disabled GET snapshot/issues still return 200 and the named read services keep history readable; there is no write route, POST returns 405. An earlier candidate asserted 403 for the disabled HTTP path, which contradicted the spec and was corrected.
Offset: PH-241 is in_review and not a dependency; the snapshot exposes offset_implemented=false (and a per-row offset placeholder note) and never invents an offset fact, per the spec.

The snapshot is derived per request from existing owner facts/read helpers; it adds no table, migration, receipt, session persistence or generic audit write (the spec made the audit optional, so the read path stays side-effect free).

Refund/return reverse cash facts are intentionally unclassified and covered by the Refund/BankReturn fact; they are marked derived_cash=refund/bank_return and excluded from classification_missing so the gold case stays issues=[].
No verify_integrity assertion was changed or added; issue codes are aligned to the existing cash verification vocabulary but the snapshot does not mutate or extend the command.

Single worker owns the whole write set (cash reconciliation service/views/template/domain metadata, delivery urls, two test files, governance); no parallel slice writes these files; independent review is pending.

The >1-active-classification issue branch is kept as defence in depth although the single-active unique constraint makes it unreachable through the owner services (comment added); no behaviour change.
